messages:
maria: quick idea — prototype for time-windowed routing syntax for gateway. Thoughts on how it should interact with host/path precedence?

maria: sketch:
```
- match:
    host: "*.example.com"
    path: "/promo/*"
    when:
      time_window:
        start: "22:00"
        end: "06:00"
    override:
      service: promo-v2
```

jake: neat. Question — if there's an explicit host route for beta.example.com + same path, which wins against the wildcard + time window?

lauren: my preference: explicit host > host wildcard. But where does "when" fit? does it raise priority? :thinking:

maria: proposal: treat when as a guard (AND condition) not a priority modifier. Precedence rules stay the same; when simply gates whether route is eligible.

ryan: telemetry note — we need to record which guard matched (e.g., matched_guard: time_window) so console can show why a request went to promo-v2.

lauren: +1 on matched_guard. Also need clear semantics for overlapping windows (22:00-06:00 crosses midnight) and tenant timezones.

maria: defaults to UTC; allow optional tenant.tz. Also allow cron-like qualifiers (e.g., weekdays) later.

jake: canaries: do we let weight-based canaries live inside when? e.g. when: time_window + weight: 10 -> only 10% during window. Combine guards with AND?

maria: think simplest: when is a list of guards ANDed. For ORs, let users create multiple routes. Keep engine simple.

lauren: agree; ORs explode config complexity. Also add a fallback block to refer to fallback route when guards fail.

maria: good call. Example fallback:
```
- match: ...
  when: ...
  override: promo-v2
  fallback: promo-v1
```

ryan: console UX: simulator that lets you input timestamp + headers + host to preview which route matches. Also show attribution in traces and per-route metrics for time-windowed slices.

infra-bot: deploy 2401234600 created for branch 'time-window-routing-proto' (CI)

jake: perf concern — evaluating time windows per request at scale must be super cheap. Precompile route time masks per region/time-slot.

maria: noted. We'll precompute bitmasks and short-circuit common cases. Also track evaluation cost in perf tests :shipit:

lauren: edgecase — legacy header-based overrides where header only present at edge. Need consistent ordering: header anchors still act as higher specificity.

maria: ok: final rough precedence rules I'll put in RFC draft:
1) explicit host > host wildcard > host-less
2) within same host: exact path > longest prefix > wildcard
3) header anchors increase specificity (treated like additional path segments)
4) when clauses are guards (no change to numeric precedence)
5) ties resolved by route weight then deployment time

maria: I'll open the RFC with examples + simulator link and tag y'all. https://git.redwood/rfcs/route-time-windows

ryan: thanks — will sketch telemetry schema for matched_guard and time_window labels.

lauren: ok, will mock console wireframes.

maria: thanks all — follow-up in RFC. :thumbsup:
